title: On Neptune, It Rains Diamonds

scenes.text: Deep inside Neptune and Uranus, the pressure is millions of times higher than on Earth.
That pressure squeezes methane so hard that its carbon atoms lock together into diamond.
The diamonds then sink through the planet for thousands of years, like rain falling through a sky of hot, dense ice.
In 2017, scientists recreated it in a lab, firing lasers at plastic and watching diamonds form in a fraction of a second.
Somewhere out there, right now, it's raining jewels.

description:
Inside Neptune and Uranus, extreme pressure turns methane into diamonds that slowly sink toward the core.
In 2017 scientists reproduced the effect in a lab using powerful lasers.
Would you want a piece of Neptune?
